items.title: OpenAI Releases Manuscript Claiming Matrix Multiplication Exponent Is Exactly 9/4
items.summary: On Nov 24 OpenAI added a preprint titled 'The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths' to its public math repository alongside Lean formalizations; the repo now holds 730 manuscripts produced by an internal model. The paper claims the exponent equals 9/4 over every field: the upper bound was already known, and the new work argues a matching lower bound, asserting that any exact arithmetic circuit for n-by-n multiplication needs at least n^(9/4)/2 multiplication or division gates. The proof links a smaller exponent to tensor-network compression that would violate a lower bound for testing whether entries in independent lists are distinct. OpenAI calls the collection raw research data rather than polished papers, warns that some unformalized results may contain issues, and defers credit and precedence to the mathematics community. Independent verification is still pending.
items.impact: A settled exponent would close a decades-old open problem and sharpen the theoretical floor for every matrix-heavy algorithm. The practical payoff is uncertain: the exponent describes asymptotic scaling, not real-world kernel speed, and the claim still needs independent review.

items.title: Nvidia Halts Server Shipments to Four Southeast Asian Markets as Export Rules Tighten
items.summary: Citing the Financial Times, The Decoder reported on Nov 26 that Nvidia told manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The pause follows US Commerce Department rules aimed at blocking companies from renting AI computing power through foreign cloud providers. Cloud providers in the four markets have 90 days to apply for licenses and prove no restricted end users are involved; one executive called the process chaotic because of missing guidance. CNBC reported thousands of Nvidia B300 chips listed for sale as dealers seek new buyers, and banks froze about $500 million in loans to Singapore-based provider Aolani for a planned ByteDance deal. Nvidia has not said whether the shipment halt is temporary or permanent.
items.impact: The rules turn third-country cloud access into a compliance bottleneck and reshape where AI capacity gets built. Expect higher costs, stalled data-center projects and a growing secondary GPU market, with knock-on effects for startups reliant on cheap regional compute.

items.title: Microsoft Warns Nation-State and Criminal Groups Are Running Attacks With ARTEX AI Agents
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a Nov 25 analysis of ARTEX, an agentic AI penetration-testing framework released in July that it says is now used by state-backed groups including Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon, Onyx Sleet and Storm-0940, plus financially motivated cybercriminals. ARTEX adds no new exploit techniques; instead, specialized agents break goals into subgoals, plan from a knowledge graph and drive existing tools such as Nmap, Sqlmap, Metasploit and headless browsers with little human oversight, automatically swapping models or API keys on failure. Microsoft logged more than 151,000 failed logins in one campaign, peaking at 2,900 per minute, and watched an agent move from exposed GitHub credentials to Azure Key Vault data in five minutes. It recommends rate limits, decoys, tarpits and convincing 'fake wins' that make agents stop attacking.
items.impact: Autonomous tooling compresses the gap between reconnaissance and breach from hours to minutes, outpacing manual triage. Defenders need behavior-based detection and automated isolation, since static indicators such as user agents are easily rotated by attackers.

items.title: CISA Adds Exploited Drupal 'Fail2Install' RCE to KEV Ahead of Nov 27 Deadline
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-132165, a remote-code-execution flaw in Drupal core, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 24, with federal remediation due Nov 27. Nicknamed Fail2Install and rated CVSS 9.8, the bug affects Drupal 8.9, 9, 10 and 11 and is classified as 'not failing securely': temporary database failures can make an installed site look uninstalled, letting an unauthenticated attacker re-enter install.php, create an administrator account or plant PHP code. Drupal patched it on Nov 18 in SA-CORE-2026-017 (versions 11.4.13, 11.3.22 and 10.6.22), and its security team saw exploitation on live sites from Nov 19. Searchlight Cyber published the exploit chain after the flaw was independently found by Anthropic's OSS scanner; no attacker has been publicly attributed.
items.impact: Drupal underpins many government, university and enterprise sites, and a KEV listing puts the flaw into automated scanners quickly. Legacy branches have no fix, so owners must move to a supported release and check logs for new admin accounts.

items.title: 42 State Attorneys General Oppose Character.AI Auction of 21 Million Users' Private Chats
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Nov 24 that a bipartisan coalition of 42 attorneys general asked a bankruptcy court to reject Character.AI's plan to sell its platform and the private chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts, including over 2.1 million registered to minors. The Dec 1 auction would include IP addresses, metadata and risk scores attached to conversations that sometimes touched self-harm, eating disorders and suicidal thoughts, despite the company having told users it did not sell personal information. The only disclosed bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed in Delaware on Nov 13 and would not be bound by Character.AI's privacy policy. The states also ask the court to reject a $350,000 break-up fee.
items.impact: The case tests whether bankruptcy can override privacy promises and child-safety laws. A ruling could set terms for data sales in future AI insolvencies, pushing courts to treat chat logs as sensitive assets rather than ordinary inventory.
